name: Venus Flytrap
description: Generates action potentials propagating at 10 cm/s triggering snap closure in 100ms. Counting mechanism requires two trigger hair touches within 20 seconds. Digestive glands activate on the fifth signal.

core_attributes.pattern: action potential generation, touch-counting memory, rapid mechanical response

scope.definition: Prey capture success rate of Dionaea muscipula — fraction of trap trigger events (two trigger hair stimulations within 30 seconds) that result in complete prey capture and digestion initiation.

evidence.source: Forterre et al. (2005) 'How the Venus flytrap snaps', Nature 433:421-425; Böhm et al. (2016) 'The Venus flytrap Dionaea muscipula counts prey-induced action potentials to induce sodium uptake', Current Biology 26:286-295.
cross_domain_examples: Venus flytrap snaps in 100-300 ms using elastic stored energy — fastest plant movement known
two-trigger requirement reduces false closures by 75% — action potential counting prevents wasted energy
snap trap mechanism confirmed as elastic energy release (buckling) not actomyosin — unique plant motor

scope.falsifiability: If single-trigger stimulation results in snap closure at equal rates to two-trigger stimulation, the two-event counting mechanism is not operating.
scope.measurement_limits: Capture efficiency decreases with trap age — each trap closes 7-10 times before senescence. Non-prey captures (rain drops, debris) open spontaneously within hours — counting mechanism reduces but doesn't eliminate false positives.
